transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
President Trump confirms former American detainee Stephen Hubbard and his family are returning
home from Russia.
On social media today, Trump hosted a picture of the group inside a plane.
Trump had issued a personal appeal for Hubbard's release, which was announced as Russian President
Vladimir Putin was meeting with White House envoy Steve Witkov about ending Russia's war
with Ukraine.
More on this from NPR's Charles Maines in Moscow.
As the talks got underway, Witkov thanked Putin for the release of 74-year-old Michigan
native Stephen Hubbard and praised Putin as a humanitarian.
The U.S. formally designated Hubbard wrongfully detained after Russian forces seized him from
his adopted home in Ukraine and later convicted him of being a Ukrainian mercenary.
His release follows a series of moves by the Trump White House aimed at easing sanctions
on Russia, decisions that have angered Ukraine and its European allies.
Trump counters the gestures of kept Russia at the negotiating table and following the
meetings with Witkov, the Kremlin announced Putin had agreed to resuscitate trilateral
peace talks with the U.S. and Ukraine.
Charles Maines, NPR News, Moscow.
Voters in Texas have less than two weeks to cast their ballot for the midterm elections.
The Texas newsroom's Blaze Ganey visited a polling location yesterday to hear from voters.
Early voting began Monday and so far turnout in several counties has outpaced the 2022
midterms.
Here in Austin, lines at several polling locations were up to an hour wait.
Voter Stacey Vakari is a life coach who usually cast her ballot during her lunch break.
"I'm like in here in five minutes and today there's a nice long line.
I'm happy to see it.
I'm happy to have to come back tomorrow because so many people are voting."
Vakari says she believes the busy polls must be a sign that Texas voters are sick of the
current Republican administration in getting out to vote for Democrats.
In the state's high-profile Senate race, polls show Democratic candidate James Tallarico
ahead of Texas Attorney General Ken Paxson.
For NPR News, I'm Blaze Ganey in Austin.
A serious security vulnerability in a popular programming language has website operators
around the globe scrambling to protect their web pages.
The language, called PHP, quietly supports components of major platforms like WordPress
and Drupal.
Some estimates suggest PHP is used to power close to 70% of modern web pages.
Government agencies in the Netherlands and Finland, for example, took their websites
offline to preempt any attacks.
Major technology companies were involved in uncovering the flaw, including OpenAI, which
said in a blog post that its model helped find the bug before attackers did.
Developers maintaining the programming language release patches to seal the hole on Wednesday.
The NSA urged organizations to take their systems down and apply the fix immediately.
Jenna McLaughlin, NPR News.
This is NPR.
New York City congressional candidate Brad Lander tells NPR's Here and Now that he was
briefly detained today by the Israeli military alongside Americans and Israeli rabbis in
the occupied West Bank.
He says they were part of a group harvesting olives to support Palestinian farmers unable
to reach olive groves under threat of violence from Israeli settlers.
NFL commissioner Roger Goodell says the league welcomes an investigation into whether the
Philadelphia Eagles did enough to protect the well-being of quarterback Jalen Hertz,
who's been diagnosed with multiple blood clots.
The NFL Players Association had called for a full investigation.
Actor Christina Applegate says it turns out she does not have multiple sclerosis.
She says neurologists informed her that she was misdiagnosed five years ago.
Her story is not uncommon, NPR's Kristen Wright explains.
Christina Applegate shared her anguish at the misdiagnosis on her podcast Messy, where
she and co-host Jamie Lynn Sigler talk about living with MS.
I'm back at square one that I don't know what's going on with me.
Full sclerosis is hard to diagnose because there is no single test and symptoms mimic
other diseases.
It's diagnosed with a list of criteria and by ruling out other conditions.
Specialist Dr. Marwa Casey said on the podcast her own study found one in five patients had
been misdiagnosed with the autoimmune disease.
Some of those criteria are still a little bit subjective and those criteria change every
seven or so years and so you really have to stay on top of the latest.
Applegate says her doctors are working on a new diagnosis.
Kristen Wright reporting, it's NPR.

topics.text: Trump confirms former detainee Stephen Hubbard and his family are returning home from Russia
Texas voters line up at Austin polls as early voting turnout outpaces 2022 midterms
Serious PHP programming language flaw prompts website operators worldwide to scramble for patches
Brad Lander says he was briefly detained by Israeli military in occupied West Bank
NFL's Roger Goodell welcomes investigation into Eagles' handling of quarterback Jalen Hurts' blood clots
Christina Applegate says she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis five years ago
